Lightning → Bitcoin

Getting onto Lightning is safe and locked down. Your Lightning lives in your own node, inside this app, under your own seed phrase. Nobody else can touch it, and using this bridge doesn't change that.

Once your sats are on Lightning, the choice is yours — and it stays yours. Hold them on Lightning: fast, cheap, and complete in itself. Or push them out to Bitcoin mainnet here — to your own Fluid Bitcoin address by default, or to another wallet if you choose. Neither is pushed. Both stay available whenever you want them.

Read this before you cross

Two steps, two systems. Step 1 swaps your Lightning sats into Arkade — a Bitcoin layer-2 run with the Arkade operator (arkade.computer) — through Satora, atomically: the swap either completes, or the Lightning payment fails back and nothing moves. Step 2 exits Arkade to your Bitcoin address in the operator's next batch.

Arkade is new software. The Arkade protocol and its operator are pre-1.0 and live only since 2025 — real, but not battle-tested like Bitcoin itself. Treat this bridge as a crossing, not a vault: move sats across, don't store them here.

The operator can never take your coins. The operator coordinates exits in batches and co-signs them, but your coins sit in outputs whose exit transactions are pre-signed by you. If the operator disappeared, you could still exit on your own after a waiting period (about a week) — slower, and it costs a normal Bitcoin network fee, but the coins stay yours. The one thing the operator must be alive for is the cheap, fast batched exit — and for renewals.

Arkade coins expire. Every Arkade balance has an expiry (about a month — yours is shown below). Past it, unspent coins can be swept by the operator. Fluid shows your deadline and offers a renewal, but don't leave sats parked in Arkade.

Costs are read live and shown before you confirm: Satora's swap fee (0.15% + 1 sat when last checked), the Arkade exit fee (a flat per-exit charge plus up to 0.2%, set by the operator), and Fluid's own fee on the swap step only, capped by Fluid's fee law. The exit fee goes entirely to the Arkade operator — Fluid earns nothing on the exit.

Irreversible steps. Once the swap's Lightning invoice is paid, that step can't be undone. Once an exit is submitted to a batch, it can't be recalled. Check the destination Bitcoin address carefully — a wrong address loses the money.

Batches take minutes, not seconds. The exit lands in the operator's next batch, then confirms on Bitcoin like any other transaction.

Settings & safety

The backup file is only as strong as your password — anyone who gets the file can guess at it offline, for as long as it takes. Guard it like the seed phrase.

Connect Fluid to other apps (dApps) that offer WalletConnect. You review and approve every connection and every signature here in Fluid — nothing is ever signed sight unseen.

Agentic wallet

Give an AI agent its own wallet on Fluid. Agents get full blockchain access — every chain — with no KYC and no on/off-ramps, ever. The agent wallet is a separate account from yours (same seed backup), with spending caps you set. The agent can only request transfers; you approve and Fluid signs.

Hand this descriptor to your agent — it contains only public addresses and its rules, never keys:
